claims.claim: The Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms.
claims.episode_span: President Trump has rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire
claims.source_title: Report: Trump rejects Iran's ceasefire proposal, may resume bombing after midterms
claims.supporting_quote: President Trump has rejected Iran’s proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms, The Wall Street Journal reported.

claims.claim: Officials cited by the Wall Street Journal said Trump is reluctant to resume major combat operations, that his views could change, and that midterm results could sway him.
claims.episode_span: he is reluctant to resume major combat operations, that his views could change, and that the midterm results could sway him
claims.source_title: Report: Trump rejects Iran's ceasefire proposal, may resume bombing after midterms
claims.supporting_quote: Citing officials, the newspaper reported that Trump is reluctant to resume major combat operations, while noting his views could change and that he could also end up being swayed by the midterm results.

claims.claim: Tehran's proposal would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz and resumed nuclear talks if the United States lifted its blockade of Iranian ports, which is causing deep damage to Iran's economy.
claims.episode_span: Tehran's proposal would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz and resumed nuclear talks in return for the United States lifting its blockade of Iranian ports.
claims.source_title: Report: Trump rejects Iran's ceasefire proposal, may resume bombing after midterms
claims.supporting_quote: Tehran’s proposal would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz and resumed nuclear talks in return for the US lifting its blockade of Iranian ports, which is causing deep damage to the country’s economy.

claims.claim: On Friday the UN human rights office added 61 companies to a database that now includes 214 firms operating in Israeli West Bank settlements, which the UN considers illegal.
claims.episode_span: added 61 companies to its database of firms operating in Israeli West Bank settlements, which the UN considers illegal
claims.source_title: UN expands list of companies operating in West Bank settlements
claims.supporting_quote: The United Nations human rights office issued a list on Friday adding 61 more companies operating in Israeli West Bank settlements, which the global body considers illegal.

claims.claim: The database, first released in 2020, includes firms mostly from Israel and also from 10 other countries including France, Germany, China and the United States, in territory home to over 3 million Palestinians.
claims.episode_span: the database now lists 214 firms, mostly from Israel, and also from 10 other countries including France, Germany, China and the United States
claims.source_title: UN expands list of companies operating in West Bank settlements
claims.supporting_quote: The database, first released in 2020, now includes 214 firms, mostly from Israel, but also from 10 other countries including France, Germany, China and the US.

claims.claim: Newly listed firms include ADAMA, part of Chinese-owned Syngenta Group, Alony Hetz, and Spain's Salvat Logistica, joining Expedia and Airbnb, and the new firms did not immediately comment.
claims.episode_span: Newly added names include Israeli pesticides maker ADAMA, part of Chinese-owned Syngenta Group, the Israel-based real estate holding company Alony Hetz, and Spain's Salvat Logistica.
claims.source_title: UN expands list of companies operating in West Bank settlements
claims.supporting_quote: Newly added firms included Israeli pesticides maker ADAMA, part of Chinese-owned Syngenta Group, Israel-based real estate investment holding company Alony Hetz and Spain's Salvat Logistica.

claims.claim: On Friday in New York, during the 81st UN General Assembly, Han Zheng told John Dramani Mahama that China is ready to deepen the China-Ghana strategic partnership, including mining, green energy, vocational training and youth development, and urged use of a zero-tariff policy.

claims.claim: Mahama said Ghana adheres to the one-China policy and wants cooperation in trade, investment, mining, manufacturing and people-to-people exchanges.

claims.supporting_quote: Ghana always adheres to the one-China policy and looks forward to strengthening cooperation with China in fields such as trade, investment, mining and manufacturing, and enhancing people-to-people exchanges to continuously enrich bilateral relations, Mahama said.

claims.claim: Turki Al-Maliki said air defences shot down two Houthi drones toward the Riyadh area and two ballistic missiles targeting Khamis Mushait.
